Car

class Car(settings)[source]

Bases: object

Car controlled by the player (feet position via MediaPipe).

Parameters:
settingsGameSettings

Game configuration (injected).

Attributes:
settingsGameSettings

Game configuration.

orig_imagepygame.Surface

Vehicle image at CAR_SIZE.

imagepygame.Surface

Image drawn (copy of orig_image).

image_smallerpygame.Surface

Vehicle image loaded again at CAR_SIZE.

rectpygame.Rect

Collision rectangle (hitbox), CAR_HITBOX_SIZE.

left_clickbool

Interaction control (click / feet closed).

lane_historycollections.deque

(time, lane) pairs of the last COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCE seconds; with tolerance 0, only the current lane.

draw

Draw the car on screen, centered on its hitbox.

record_lane(lane, now=None)[source]

Record the current lane of the player (called every frame).

Parameters:
laneint

Current lane (0, 1, 2; -1 outside the area).

nowfloat | None, optional

Timestamp (s); time.time() when None.

Notes

Entries older than COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCE are dropped, but the most recent one is always kept.

hits(target)[source]

Decide whether the object hits the car, by player lane.

Considers the lanes recorded in the tolerance window (GameSettings.COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCE): it collides if the player was in the object’s lane (star or obstacle) for MOST of the window. This absorbs the jitter of the feet reading near the lane boundary in both directions: a player in the lane does not miss the collision because of one wrong frame, and a player in another lane does not collide because of one frame read in the object’s lane.

Parameters:
targetTarget

Object reaching the car.

Returns:
bool

True if it collides. With tolerance 0 the lane at the instant of the passage counts. Outside the area (-1) it does not collide.

Examples

>>> from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
>>> car = Car.__new__(Car)
>>> car.settings = NS(COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCE=0.2)
>>> car.lane_history = deque()
>>> for t, lane in [(0.0, 1), (0.05, 2), (0.1, 1)]:
...     car.record_lane(lane, now=t)
>>> car.hits(NS(current_road=1))
True
kill_targets(targets)[source]

Resolve the collisions of the objects that reached the car.

When the base of an object passes the front of the car (top of the hitbox) in this frame, it collides if the player is in the object’s lane (see hits). If it does not collide, the object goes on and is recorded as avoided when it leaves the screen (GameController).

Parameters:
targetslist

Active objects; collided ones are removed from it.

Returns:
list[KillResult]

One result per object collided in this frame. Score, recording and feedback are handled by GameController.
